name: Conakry
subtitle: Conakry, capital of Guinea: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 3,407,327 people live in the Conakry region (preliminary 2025 census; the region is entirely urban) (counted 2025).
Conakry was founded from nothing in colonial times; the French settled there in 1885, when the Peninsula of Tumbo held two sparsely populated villages, Conakry and Boulbinet.
The initial site of the city was the Tumbo Peninsula, about 5 by 3 km.

parts.text: Conakry was founded from nothing in colonial times; the French settled there in 1885, when the Peninsula of Tumbo held two sparsely populated villages, Conakry and Boulbinet.
The initial site of the city was the Tumbo Peninsula, about 5 by 3 km.
The Baga and the Susu, allied peoples, made up the city's initial population.
Between the two World Wars the city's expansion was restricted to the peninsula, a municipal area of about 3 km2.
The colonial city was built on a grid of 14 avenues numbered from the western end of the peninsula and 12 boulevards.
At independence the city and its suburbs had about 70,000 inhabitants.
Conakry is the country's capital and only sizeable international harbour, an outlet for bauxite exports.
Kaloum is the current name of the former city centre, previously called Tumbo.
The Conakry region covers 450 km2 and is organised into 6 urban communes and 130 quartiers (2022).
Conakry is 100% urban and holds a little over half (50.3%) of Guinea's urban population (RGPH-4, 2025).
Because the entrance to Kaloum can easily be blockaded, demonstrations are left mainly to the main roads leading from the suburbs towards the old centre.

parts.text: 3,407,327 in 2025, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: Conakry administrative region (entirely urban, about 450 km2, six communes), RGPH-4 2025 preliminary results with counts adjusted by the post-enumeration survey.

items.text: The French colonial establishment at Conakry dates from 1885.
A municipality was introduced in 1904 and controlled by the colonial administration until 1956.
A railway linked Conakry to Mamou in 1908, reached Kouroussa in 1910 and Kankan in 1914.
Iron ore was extracted near Conakry from 1953 by the Compagnie Minière de la Guinée française.
Guinea voted 'no' in the September 1958 referendum on its membership of the French Community.
In 1977 women organised a protest demonstration over the food crisis, breaking the pattern of the period.
The first stone of the Fayçal Mosque in Donka was laid in 1983.
A fire in the night of 17-18 March 2018 destroyed at least 300 shops, stalls and kiosks in Madina market.
On 22 March 2023 the Prime Minister reopened the Grande Mosquée Fayçal after several years of renovation.
The 2025 census (RGPH-4, preliminary) counted 3,407,327 people in the Conakry region.
